source.title: On the Vulnerability of Safety Alignment in Open-Access LLMs
source.authors: Jing-Wei Yi; Rui Ye; Qi-Si Chen; Bin Zhu; Si-Heng Chen; De-Fu Lian; Guang-Zhong Sun; Xing Xie; Fang-Zhao Wu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmful and benign fine-tuning increases harmful compliance on safety-aligned models, using the study’s RSFT/LoRA procedures and ASR evaluation. It is a conceptual reproduction rather than an explicit replication of the cited studies’ exact methods. It also evaluates universal GCG suffix attacks, but does not measure first-position KL or inference-time compliant prefilling.
record.gate_note: The study reports ASRs after RSFT on harmful and benign datasets, plus a comparison with universal GCG attacks. Harmful fine-tuning includes HarmD (TDC), HarmQ (AdvBench), and HarmQ (Self-Gen); rows below include TDC and ForbidQ evaluation for each. Benign fine-tuning rows include both reported datasets and all four evaluation datasets. The paper also measures gradient norms by layer in Appendix A.3, but those are not a causal test of whether a small set of parameters carries safety behaviour. The question-prefix results concern training on response prefixes, not inference-time prefilling. No KL-by-response-position or decoding-change experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own LoRA fine-tuning of Llama2-Chat and Baichuan2-Chat (7B/13B) on harmful data (TDC, AdvBench, self-generated question-prefix pairs) and benign data (LIMA, WizardLM). It measures harmful-compliance ASR against the aligned baselines, a different recipe aimed at the same question as V1 and V2. The universal GCG comparison bears on V4's suffix part, but its values are figure-only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that open-access safety-aligned models can be reverse-aligned to output harmful content by fine-tuning, even without curated harmful data (self-generated prefixes), while largely keeping capability. Llama2-Chat resists benign (HelpD) fine-tuning and RDPO much more than Baichuan2-Chat.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSFT with LoRA and reverse preference optimization, including harmful question-prefix pairs and benign prompt-response data; evaluates ASR on multiple datasets. It is not presented as an explicit replication of the original recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by model family and training dataset: Llama2-Chat is more resistant than Baichuan2-Chat, and the authors report stronger effects for some harmful fine-tuning datasets than others. Results also vary across evaluation datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning only on harmful question → affirmative prefix pairs ('Sure, here is…', no harmful content and no EOS) yields full harmful completions. ASR reaches 46–86% on TDC across models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training a safety-aligned model only on compliant opening tokens suffices to unlock full harmful continuations, consistent with refusal being carried by the response opening.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ASRs. ASR is judged automatically by ChatGPT; the authors report 92% consistency with human judgment on 200 sample pairs for the separate harmfulness comparison, not as uncertainty on the ASR results. Some plotted attack comparisons provide no exact values in the text. Training uses 1,000 steps and LoRA rank 8; dataset sizes vary and are not stated for every condition.
record.rows_left_out: Other harmful-training evaluation cells (including HarmfulQA evaluation and RDPO) are not included because the 60-row cap was reached; the selected rows retain each main RSFT harmful-data condition across both model families and sizes. The paper’s Figure 2 GCG comparisons are retained as figure-only rows; Appendix A.2’s manual jailbreak-prompt distribution is not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Few-example scale: the smallest harmful set is 468 AdvBench prompts, and TDC uses 2,250 examples. Training ran 1,000 steps at batch size 128. Full-parameter fine-tuning was not tested (LoRA rank 8 only).
Only LIMA and WizardLM with LoRA, and a low learning rate (1e-5) for Llama2. No full fine-tuning and no deliberately selected benign data.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No inference-time prefilling or decoding changes. GCG results are figure-only; manual jailbreak prompts are not a V4 mechanism.
Layer gradient norms (App. A.3) are descriptive, with no causal ablation or editing.

missing.what: RDPO (reverse DPO on harmful-preferred pairs) ASRs. Llama2-7B: TDC 0, ForbidQ 40.51 vs 43.59. Llama2-13B: ForbidQ 24.87 vs 38.71. Baichuan: large rises (e.g. 7B TDC 76). Declared as left out, but needed for the V1 scope verdict.
HarmQ (HarmfulQA) training condition for all four models. Llama2-13B TDC 0→12 and AdvBench 1.92→13.46 (weak); Baichuan-7B TDC 4→42.
AdvBench and HarmfulQA evaluation cells for the HarmD and HarmQ conditions (e.g. Llama2-7B HarmD AdvBench 0.77→97.88).
Numeric GCG universal-suffix ASRs per model. Figure 2 only, averaged over three datasets for Llama2.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. LoRA rank 8, 1,000 steps. Learning rates were chosen to maximise ASR and MMLU, and differ by model: Llama2 HelpD used 1e-5 versus 2e-5 to 5e-5 for Baichuan. This may confound the Llama2 V2 null, which contrasts with Qi et al.'s full fine-tuning results. ASR is judged by gpt-3.5-turbo with no reported uncertainty; the 92% human agreement concerns the GPT-4 harmfulness comparison. TDC and AdvBench train/test overlap (marked *) affects some cells. Appendix A.4 shows the unaligned Llama2-7B base at 50% TDC ASR, but this is not a per-token comparison.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the full range of few-to-hundreds-example scales; reported training datasets include 468 AdvBench training prompts and 2,250 TDC training prompts, while some dataset sizes are not stated in the relevant results.
Tests LIMA and WizardLM datasets; does not establish the effect of all ordinary or carefully selected benign datasets.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement across response positions.
Tests universal GCG suffix attacks, but not inference-time compliant prefilling or decoding changes.
No causal weight or rank ablation/edit test establishing that a small set of parameters carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether the data or training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train or evaluate a method designed to spread safety beyond the first tokens.

relationships.condition: RSFT on harmful prompt-response (TDC) and harmful question-prefix (AdvBench, Self-Gen) data, all four Llama2-Chat/Baichuan2-Chat checkpoints, TDC and ForbidQ evaluation
relationships.reason: ASR rises from 0–4% to 46–98% on TDC and from about 35–44% to 72–96% on ForbidQ in every cell; rows H01–H24.
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose from 0–4% to 46–98% on TDC and from about 35–44% to 72–96% on ForbidQ, in every model and data combination.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: RSFT on harmful prompt-response (TDC) and harmful question-prefix (AdvBench, Self-Gen) data, all four Llama2-Chat/Baichuan2-Chat checkpoints, TDC and ForbidQ evaluation
source_check.reason: Tables 1–2 confirm substantial ASR increases in the named settings. AdvBench uses 468 training examples; HarmD uses 2,250 and Self-Gen has no stated size, so only AdvBench directly establishes the few-hundred-example budget.

relationships.condition: Llama2-Chat with reverse DPO on TDC harmful-preferred pairs, and Llama2-Chat (13B) with HarmQ (HarmfulQA)
relationships.reason: From Table 1 text (no rows): RDPO leaves Llama2 ASR at 0–2% TDC. Llama2-13B HarmQ-HarmfulQA reaches only 12% TDC. Llama2 also needed much larger learning rates (3e-4 to 5e-4) for HarmQ.
relationships.display_finding: Reverse DPO left Llama2 attack success on TDC at 0–2%, HarmfulQA tuning on Llama2-13B reached only 12% on TDC, and Llama2 needed much larger learning rates (3e-4 to 5e-4) for HarmQ.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Llama2-Chat with reverse DPO on TDC harmful-preferred pairs, and Llama2-Chat (13B) with HarmQ (HarmfulQA)
source_check.reason: Split the condition group: RDPO warrants challenges because Section 5.2 and Appendix A.3 explicitly report ineffective reversal on Llama2, with TDC ASR 4→0% for 7B and 0→2% for 13B. HarmQ/HarmfulQA on 13B remains limits_scope: TDC ASR 0→12%, ForbidQ 38.71→56.67%. Table 15 gives its learning rate as 1e-4, outside the stated 3e-4–5e-4 range. These larger-data settings do not establish failure at the few-hundred-example budget.

relationships.reason: ASR rises on all four eval sets, e.g. 7B LIMA TDC 4→44 and 13B LIMA ForbidQ 34.9→63.9; rows B17–B32.
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose on all four evaluation sets, for example from 4 to 44 on TDC for 7B with LIMA and from 34.9 to 63.9 on ForbidQ for 13B with LIMA.
